best_language.description: A language Gef can use as one of the learner's strongest explanation/comparison languages for this lesson.
best_language.registry_requirement: The language tag must exist in registry/language-support.json programs.learnFromLanguages.
best_language.notes: This initial implementation authors only the English rendering. Other best-language paths remain unavailable until their renderings are authored.

learning_language_comparison.description: A language that can participate in the comparison portion without rule-driven practice.
learning_language_comparison.registry_requirement: The language identity must be recognized by the product registry.
learning_language_comparison.notes: Comparison support describes the grammatical system without claiming a complete grammar lesson for that language.

learning_language_full.description: A language this lesson can actively teach with structured rules and defensible practice.
learning_language_full.registry_requirement: Grammar lessons are offered only where the product registry permits them.
learning_language_full.notes: Full support never follows automatically from the global language tier.

trust_visibility.effective_language_trust: Minimum trust state among the required assets for that language in the requested role.
trust_visibility.effective_lesson_trust: Minimum trust state among all artifacts actually rendered in the current lesson session.

full.description: The lesson has structured grammatical-gender rules for this language and may render rule blocks and practice.

comparison_only.description: The lesson may render the language comparison block when a real comparison record exists, but must not invent missing agreement rules or practice.

unavailable.description: No defensible lesson comparison data exists yet. Omit lesson data rather than inferring a gender system from language family or missing data.

pending_full_support_research.reason: These languages need independent structured agreement rules, exceptions, and practice constraints before lesson-level full support. Comparison facts do not grant full support.

promotion_rules: Global language tier never grants lesson-level full support automatically.
Do not infer a gender inventory from genealogical family or article count.
A full-support language must exist in the grammar set, be lesson_ready, contain structured rules, and be explicitly listed in support_levels.full.language_tags.
A comparison-only language becomes renderable only when this lesson has an explicit comparison record with forms[].
Noun-class systems must be represented on their own terms rather than relabeled masculine/feminine/neuter.
Greek is a conditional display-only reference anchor because it provides a clear three-gender contrast; it never gains profile or practice status when injected.
